entities.summary:
Ludovico Maria Sforza, known to history as Ludovico il Moro, was a pivotal figure in late 15th-century Italian politics, whose ambitious diplomatic maneuvers and cultural patronage profoundly shaped the Duchy of Milan and, by extension, the course of the Italian Wars. Born into the powerful Sforza dynasty in 1452, Ludovico initially served as regent for his young nephew, Gian Galeazzo Sforza, before consolidating his own power and formally assuming the ducal title in 1494. His reign, though brief as a sovereign duke, marked a critical transition point in Italian history, moving from a period of relative peace under the Peace of Lodi to an era of devastating foreign intervention.

Ludovico's rise to power was characterized by shrewd political maneuvering, including the suspicious death of Gian Galeazzo in 1494, which cemented his ducal claim. His most fateful decision, however, was inviting King Charles VIII of France to invade Italy in 1494, hoping to use French military might to counter the growing influence of Naples and Venice. This invitation inadvertently opened the floodgates, initiating a series of French incursions that would engulf the peninsula for decades. Despite his initial success in maneuvering between great powers, Ludovico's alliances proved fickle. He later joined the League of Venice against Charles VIII but faced a new threat when Louis XII, Charles's successor, asserted his own claim to Milan through his Visconti ancestry.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Ludovico Sforza's invitation to Charles VIII in 1494 directly triggered the French invasion of Italy, initiating decades of devastating Italian Wars that reshaped the European balance of power, while his patronage fostered a golden age of art and science in Milan.
